Why (one line): Cheapest overall. Decent hiking and museums.
What a week looks like: Saguaro NP: Wasson Peak (Hugh Norris or King Canyon trail). Sabino Canyon / Seven Falls; Mt Lemmon if there's no snow. Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum, Pima Air & Space, Mission San Xavier del Bac. Sonoran hot dogs, carne asada, a UNESCO City of Gastronomy food scene.
Girlfriend: DTW flight (Jan 5-12): DTW-LAX about 11.9h with 1 stop (Frontier, $254 RT), then drive together

Why (one line): Best mix of big hikes and a world-class museum/food city, and the cheapest, easiest meetup for both.
What a week looks like: Museo Nacional de Antropologia, Frida Kahlo/Coyoacan, Bellas Artes, Teotihuacan. Big hike: La Malinche summit (7.9 mi, 4,320 ft, 14,600 ft altitude; acclimatize, maybe hire a guide, possible ice). Shorter: Tepozteco or Desierto de los Leones. (Ajusco dropped: see Safety tab.) Tacos, mercados, one splurge dinner (Pujol or Contramar).
Card & points (estimate, short): Pay cash with Sapphire Preferred (CSP); Credit Max's Virgin/Aeromexico award (about $460 in points) doesn't beat the $487 fare.

Why (one line): Mexico's best food and crafts city with real mountain hiking. Warmest of the city picks.
What a week looks like: Museo de las Culturas at Santo Domingo, the Ethnobotanical Garden, Monte Alban, Mitla, Hierve el Agua. Big hike: guided Sierra Norte Cuajimoloyas to Latuvi (10.1 mi, 6.5-7h). Mole, tlayudas, mercado food, mezcal; reserve one dinner (e.g. Criollo or Casa Oaxaca).
US State Dept advisory: Level 2 (Isthmus region restricted, far from the city)
Card & points (estimate, short): Cash with CSP; the Aeromexico award (about $460) is roughly break-even.

Why (one line): Cheap, and no weather penalty now, but a thin museum/food scene.
What a week looks like: Joshua Tree: Ryan Mountain, Lost Palms Oasis, Hidden Valley / Skull Rock. Palm Springs Aerial Tramway to the San Jacinto trails (can be snowy). Palm Springs Art Museum, Sunnylands, Moorten Botanical Garden; date shakes, Palm Springs restaurants.
Girlfriend: DTW flight (Jan 5-12): DTW-LAX about 11.9h with 1 stop (Frontier, $254 RT). The cheapest is $224 at 19.9h.

Why (one line): Alhambra, the Seville Alcazar and Picasso museums plus tapas, with gorge and Sierra Nevada foothill hikes. Granada nights get near freezing.
What a week looks like: Malaga: Picasso Museum, Alcazaba. Caminito del Rey gorge walk (closed Mondays and Jan 11-19, 2027, so book Jan 6-10). Granada: Alhambra (book ahead), Albaicin; a hike in the Alpujarras or the Monachil Los Cahorros gorge. Seville: Alcazar, Cathedral, flamenco. Tapas crawls.
January weather (official normals): Seville: high ~61F / low ~43F; Granada: ~55F / ~34F (airport normals via Wikipedia)
Card & points (estimate, short): Maybe: Iberia Avios to Madrid off-peak (about 25.5k each way + $150-200 tax per person; 30% transfer bonus through Dec 1), then train south.

Why (one line): Pompeii, Herculaneum and Naples' museums plus pizza, with Vesuvius and the Path of the Gods. Mild but sometimes wet in January.
What a week looks like: Naples: National Archaeological Museum, Capodimonte, the Underground. Pompeii and Herculaneum. Hikes: Path of the Gods (Bomerano to Nocelle; real shoes, skip it in rain). Vesuvius is now a guided out-and-back to 1,170 m (the rim loop is closed; book online). Optional: Capri by ferry if seas allow. Pizza at the classics; reserve one dinner.
January weather (official normals): Naples: high ~56F / low ~40F, about 9 rain days (Naples airport 1991-2020, via Wikipedia)
Card & points (estimate, short): Maybe: United partner award (about 40k each way to Rome) for his leg.

Why (one line): Elite museums and food, mild, cheapest Europe flights for both. Hiking is moderate (day hikes, not big mountains).
What a week looks like: Gulbenkian, Azulejo Museum, MAAT, Belem. Sintra: Pena and the Moorish Castle on foot via Sintra-Cascais park trails; a coastal Arrabida day hike. Pasteis, tascas, seafood; reserve one dinner. Optional 2 nights in Porto.
Card & points (estimate, short): Maybe: United partner award (about 40k each way) for his leg. Cash is already fairly low.

Why (one line): Superb food and the National Palace Museum, mild, but Taroko's main gorge trails are closed and the flights are long for her.
What a week looks like: Taipei: National Palace Museum, night markets, Yangmingshan hikes. Day trip to Teapot Mountain / Jiufen. Tainan: old-town temples and street food. (Taroko's main gorge trails are closed.)
January weather (official normals): Taipei ~67F / ~58F, about 14 rain days; Tainan ~73F / ~58F (1991-2020 normals via Wikipedia)

Why (one line): Cheapest warm trip for both, no passport needed, a real old city plus rainforest hikes. Hikes are shorter than their usual.
What a week looks like: Old San Juan, El Morro and San Cristobal forts, Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico. El Yunque: El Toro or El Yunque peak trail (reservation for the road). Bioluminescent bay; lechon in Guavate; reserve one dinner in San Juan.
January weather (official normals): High ~83F / low ~72F, short showers on about 12 days (NOAA)
Card & points (estimate, short): Pay cash with CSP (fares already low).

Why (one line): Top-tier city food and museums with genuinely great mountain/coastal hiking. Mild and dry. Long-haul, though, and her flight is long and pricey.
What a week looks like: Hikes: Lantau Peak (sunrise), Dragon's Back, a MacLehose Trail section in Sai Kung. M+ and the Hong Kong Palace Museum, the Peak, Star Ferry. Dim sum, dai pai dong, roast goose; reserve one dinner.
January weather (official normals): High ~66F / low ~58F, about 6 rain days (Hong Kong Observatory)
Girlfriend: DTW flight (Jan 5-12): About 22h with 1 stop (United, $1,923). A $1,190 fare takes about 32h.
Card & points (estimate, short): No award estimate from Credit Max for HK. Pay cash with CSP.

Why (one line): Best pure hiking and nature (active volcano, Mauna Kea, snorkeling); weakest city/museum side.
What a week looks like: Hawaii Volcanoes NP: Kilauea Iki and Napau Crater (11.9 mi, 5-5.5h). Mauna Kea via the Humu'ula Trail (9-10h, above 12,000 ft) or the stargazing route. Captain Cook / Ka'awaloa hike (1,256 ft) plus snorkeling. Pu'uhonua o Honaunau, the 'Imiloa center in Hilo. Poke, plate lunch; reserve Merriman's Waimea.
Card & points (estimate, short): Possible saving: BA Avios on Alaska/Hawaiian, about 88k Avios for 2 LAX round trips (Credit Max estimate, about $700 value vs about $894 cash). Her DTW leg needs its own check. Verify on ba.com.

Why (one line): The best day-hiking island in Europe, mild all winter, with a pleasant small city in Funchal.
What a week looks like: PR1 Pico do Arieiro to Pico Ruivo ridge (reopened fully May 2026; booked time slot, EUR 10.50), PR9 Caldeirao Verde levada, Sao Lourenco point, 25 Fontes. Funchal old town, Mercado dos Lavradores, Monte cable car, Madeira wine lodges. Fish (espada), poncha bars.
January weather (official normals): Funchal: high ~68F / low ~58F, about 6 rain days (Funchal Observatory 1991-2020, via Wikipedia)
Card & points (estimate, short): Maybe: United partner award (about 40k each way to Lisbon) plus a Lisbon-Funchal hop. Check on United.

Why (one line): Great outdoors and easy for him, but a weak city/museum scene and a 2-stop trip from DTW.
What a week looks like: Espiritu Santo boat day, Balandra, Sierra de la Laguna; Malecon.
Card & points (estimate, short): Virgin/Aeromexico award about $280 for his leg (estimate).

Why (one line): Warmest place in Europe, with big volcano hikes. Small-city culture only (La Laguna).
What a week looks like: Teide: summit by permit (or Montana Blanca trail plus the cable car), the Roques de Garcia loop. Anaga forest ridges; Masca gorge (booking required, check status). La Laguna old town, Museo de la Naturaleza y Arqueologia. Guachinches (local wine taverns).
Card & points (estimate, short): Maybe: Iberia Avios via Madrid (Iberia flies to the Canaries).

Why (one line): Fine beach and jungle trip; Jalisco is Level 3.
What a week looks like: Coastal trail to Las Animas, Botanical Garden.
Card & points (estimate, short): Virgin/Aeromexico award about $400 for his leg (estimate).

Why (one line): Lovely, but costly lodging and not much city.
Card & points (estimate, short): BA Avios as for the Big Island.
